findings.passage: She came out as gay in seventh grade and as transgender in ninth, the 2012-13 school year. Her first two attempts did not get through; the third landed, Katy Schafer told WUNC, because "we had kind of lost our kid." Hunter finished that freshman year, at 14, in a skirt.
findings.problem: The school year is wrong on the article's own opened sources. She graduated from high school in 2017 (NYT May 2018, S10: 'After graduating from high school in 2017'; GQ, S01: senior year when HB2 was repealed in March 2017; HuffPost April 2017, S43: 'high school senior thesis'; A24: UNCSA for her last two years), so ninth grade was the 2013-14 school year, not 2012-13. Born December 31, 1998, she was 14 that fall, which matches her own 'began transitioning at 14' (Teen Vogue, S08) and GQ's 'began transitioning at age 14, and then three years later became the youngest plaintiff', and 15 by the last day of freshman year in spring 2014. '2012-13' was derived at the edit stage from Rolling Stone's compressed 'at age 14, attending her last day of her freshman year' (S27) and contradicts three other sources. The article repeats that compression twice more ('finished that freshman year, at 14, in a skirt'; 'a 14-year-old finishing freshman year in a skirt' in the closing section).
findings.acceptance_test: The body reads 'the 2013-14 school year' (or gives no year), and the two 'at 14 ... freshman year' phrasings either attribute the age to Rolling Stone or drop it (e.g. 'Hunter finished that freshman year in a skirt'; 'a ninth-grader finishing the year in a skirt' or 'a 14-year-old coming out in ninth grade'). C03's claim text states the corrected arithmetic and cites S44 (ninth grade) and S10 (2017 graduation); C90's text matches. No other date in the childhood section changes.

findings.passage: She conceded that harsh critiques from high-profile strangers "can be a bit unsettling."
findings.problem: The Orange County Register sentence is the reporter's paraphrase ('Schafer did acknowledge, however, that having high-profile strangers delivering harsh critiques ... can be a bit unsettling'), not a quotation. The quotation marks present the paraphrase as her words; C107 already records it as a paraphrase.
findings.acceptance_test: The quotation marks are removed ('can be a bit unsettling, the Register reported') or the sentence is rephrased as the paper's paraphrase; C107's passage is updated to match.

findings.passage: Twenty years later, on a podcast, in the middle of a joke about her afflictions, she described the same core in one sentence.
findings.problem: Two small unsupported precisions. ELLE gives no age for the birthday-party memory ('a young kid'), so 'Twenty years later' is a guess at the interval to the August 2024 podcast. Separately, 'Cuckoo, her first film and her first lead' is true only in shooting order (Rolling Stone: 'lapped in release by projects she filmed later, like last year's The Hunger Games'); by release, Songbirds & Snakes (November 2023) came first, and a reader will read 'first film' as release order.
findings.acceptance_test: 'Twenty years later' becomes an unquantified phrase ('Years later' / 'As an adult, on a podcast'), and 'her first film and her first lead' becomes 'the first film she shot, and her first lead' or simply 'her first lead'; C92 and C36 passages updated.

findings.passage: [Type 4](/enneagram-corner/enneagram-type-4) sits in the heart triad, the three types organized around shame. In a Four that shame looks less like embarrassment than a running comparison between the person inside and the person the world reflects back. A Four builds an inner world where the real self can live, looks for a medium that can carry it outside, and then checks whether the world saw the right thing; the usual cost is a chronic sense of being misread.
findings.problem: Length and density. The body is 4,423 words against the standard's 2,000-3,500 target (4,500 ceiling) after a repair round that every reviewer asked to be net cuts; the edit added about 430 words. The thesis is restated in several places (this four-sentence type-mechanism paragraph; 'it is the move this profile keeps finding' and the self-location restatement in the counterevidence section; 'That is the discriminator'), and the final Why-not-3 paragraph on the two revisions is dense enough to need a second read. Not a release blocker, but it is what holds the writing score below the 9 anchor.
findings.acceptance_test: The repair pass nets out at or below roughly 4,000 words without removing sourced evidence: the type-mechanism paragraph trimmed to two sentences, one of the two self-location restatements cut, and the 'two audience-facing revisions' paragraph split or shortened so each revision and its Three prediction reads in one pass.
